date: Nov 26, 2026 · Week 3 / Day 4 · Upward communication and influence

cards.title: Protect the critical path
cards.question: PCIe corner validation and a cosmetic TDR correlation study compete for one engineer. What do you ask your director to defer?
cards.selfCheck: Rank work by release exposure, decision deadline and cost of delay. Recommend a specific deferral, with a restart trigger and owner.
cards.prompt: Role-play a director who wants both tasks completed. Coach my 30-second resource tradeoff and explicit deferral request.

cards.title: Correct the green status
cards.question: A PDN resonance exceeds the agreed impedance target at a relevant load frequency, but the program dashboard is green. How do you correct it?
cards.selfCheck: Flag the discrepancy promptly; distinguish target violation from unproven functional failure. State the transient evidence needed, accountable owner and next gate.
cards.prompt: Challenge my risk-first message to a program director who expects green status. Score candor, uncertainty and actionable next steps.

cards.title: Make the cost visible
cards.question: Layout resists a crosstalk fix because it threatens routing completion. How do you gain support without directing their work?
cards.selfCheck: Compare the routing cost with downstream validation and respin exposure. Co-design a bounded mitigation and agree on evidence before requesting approval.
cards.prompt: Play a layout lead protecting schedule. Help me negotiate a bounded crosstalk mitigation with shared success criteria.

cards.title: Promise a decision, not a cure
cards.question: A VP asks you to guarantee resolution of an EM/TDR mismatch by Friday. What commitment can you credibly make?
cards.selfCheck: Commit to a discriminating test, named owner and Friday decision checkpoint, not an unknown root cause. Explain the fallback if evidence remains inconclusive.
cards.prompt: Role-play a VP pressing for certainty. Critique my commitment, confidence language and fallback without allowing evasive answers.

cards.title: Deliver the unwelcome call
cards.question: PCIe margin fails an agreed corner criterion and a proposed waiver lacks evidence. Give leadership a 30-second release recommendation.
cards.selfCheck: Lead with release impact and recommend holding the affected gate. Name the evidence gap, recovery options, decision authority and next checkpoint.
cards.prompt: Score my executive brief against Weeks 1–3: early risk, clear recommendation, tradeoff, calibrated uncertainty and explicit ask. Challenge me with schedule pressure.
